instruction:
Create a complete 18-month Business Performance, Budget, and Inventory Control Workbook for a mid-sized consumer electronics distributor.

Use realistic generated data. Work carefully, verify each worksheet before moving on, and save the finished workbook as:
Business_Performance_Control.xlsx

Create these worksheets in this order:

1. Product Master
- Create at least 40 products across Laptops, Phones, Audio, Accessories, Office Equipment, and Gaming.
- Columns: ProductID, ProductName, Category, Supplier, StandardCost, StandardPrice, ReorderLevel, CurrentStock, LeadTimeDays.
- Format as an Excel Table named ProductMaster.
- Highlight CurrentStock below ReorderLevel in red.

2. Sales Data
- Create at least 350 sales transactions dated from Jan-2024 to Jun-2025.
- Columns: OrderID, OrderDate, CustomerName, CustomerSegment, Region, Salesperson, ProductID, ProductName, Category, UnitsSold, UnitPrice, DiscountPercent, Revenue, Cost, GrossProfit, GrossMargin, OrderStatus.
- Use regions North, South, East, West; segments Consumer, SMB, Enterprise.
- Create the Excel Table first and name it SalesData.
- Add formulas after the table exists:
  - Revenue = UnitsSold × UnitPrice × (1 − DiscountPercent)
  - Cost = Revenue × realistic cost percentage
  - GrossProfit = Revenue − Cost
  - GrossMargin = IFERROR(GrossProfit / Revenue, 0)
- Apply date, currency, and percentage formats.
- Freeze the header row and auto-fit columns.

3. Monthly Budget
- Create monthly revenue and gross-profit targets for every month and region.
- Columns: Month, Region, RevenueTarget, ActualRevenue, RevenueVariance, GrossProfitTarget, ActualGrossProfit, GrossProfitVariance, TargetStatus.
- Use formulas linked to SalesData so Actual values update automatically.
- Use conditional formatting: green when target is met, red when missed.

4. Sales Summary
- Add KPI cards for Total Revenue, Total Gross Profit, Gross Margin %, Units Sold, Average Order Value, Completed Orders, Best Region, and Best Category.
- Add summaries for monthly revenue, monthly gross profit, region performance, category performance, and top 10 products.
- All totals must update from SalesData.

5. Customer Analysis
- Show revenue, gross profit, gross margin, order count, and average order value by customer segment.
- Create a Top 10 Customers by Revenue table.
- Flag customers whose revenue is above average but gross margin is below 30%.

6. Inventory & Reorder Analysis
- Link all product information from Product Master.
- Include Stock Status and Estimated Reorder Quantity.
- Stock Status rules:
  - Critical: CurrentStock below 50% of ReorderLevel
  - Reorder Soon: CurrentStock below ReorderLevel
  - Healthy: otherwise
- Highlight Critical red, Reorder Soon amber, Healthy green.

7. Executive Dashboard
- Create a polished management dashboard.
- Include KPI cards linked to Sales Summary.
- Add these charts:
  - Monthly Revenue Trend
  - Revenue by Region
  - Gross Profit by Category
  - Target vs Actual Revenue by Region
  - Top 10 Products by Revenue
  - Revenue by Customer Segment
- Use a professional blue and green theme.
- Add a “Management Insights” section with five insights derived from the created data.
- Keep the dashboard clean, readable, and suitable for a monthly management meeting.

Before finishing:
- Check for #REF!, #VALUE!, #NAME?, and blank formula results.
- Confirm every required sheet exists.
- Confirm formulas calculate correctly.
- Save the workbook and report the final sheet names and any limitations.

advanced.description: Connects a sheet to an external data source (database, web feed, folder of files) via Excel's Power Query / Get Data engine, using a connection string and query. Best-effort: complex M-code transformations built in the Power Query editor are not supported here - this covers a straightforward 'pull this external data in' case.

advanced.description: Exports a sheet as a PDF file to a given file path.

advanced.name: fetch_live_data
advanced.description: Fetches live data from an external web API (e.g. exchange rates, stock prices) and writes the result into a cell. Only use with a URL the user has explicitly named or clearly implied - never invent or guess an API URL.

Only use a connection URL the user has explicitly provided - never invent one.

advanced.name: import_unstructured_document
advanced.description: Extracts data from a PDF, image (OCR), DOCX, or TXT/CSV file already on disk and writes it into a sheet. If the source has a detected table, writes that as rows; otherwise writes the extracted text as one line per row. Only use a file path the user has explicitly provided.

advanced.name: protect_sheet
advanced.description: Locks a sheet from further edits, optionally with a password.

advanced.name: run_macro
advanced.description: Runs an existing VBA macro already present in the workbook (recorded or hand-written), by name, with optional positional arguments. Cannot write NEW VBA code into the workbook - only executes macros that already exist there.

analysis.name: scenario_builder

charts.name: position_chart
charts.description: Positions and sizes an existing chart at a specific cell location. Use this to organize dashboard layouts and prevent overlapping charts.

dashboard.name: add_shape
dashboard.description: Draws a freeform shape (rectangle, oval, rounded rectangle, arrow) on a sheet - useful for dashboard section dividers, callout boxes, or visual accents. For a clickable button wired to a macro, use add_macro_button instead.

dashboard.name: add_sparkline
dashboard.description: Adds an in-cell sparkline (small trend chart) driven by a data range - common in dashboard rows to show a per-row trend next to the numbers.

dashboard.name: arrange_dashboard_layout
dashboard.description: Audits every visible floating object on a worksheet (charts, pictures, shapes, slicers, and controls) for overlap, or reflows them into a spaced grid and verifies the result. Use after creating a dashboard or report with visual objects.

dashboard.name: delete_chart
dashboard.description: Deletes an existing chart from a sheet by name.

dashboard.name: insert_picture
dashboard.description: Places an image file (logo, icon, screenshot) onto a sheet at a given cell anchor. The image file must already exist on disk.

dashboard.name: modify_chart
dashboard.description: Changes an existing chart's type, title, or data range without deleting and recreating it.

dashboard.name: refresh_pivot_table
dashboard.description: Refreshes an existing PivotTable so it picks up changes in its source data. Call this any time source data changes after a pivot was already built - pivots do NOT auto-refresh.

data.name: filter_data
data.description: Reads a range and returns only rows matching a condition on one column. operator: 'equals', 'greater_than', 'less_than', 'contains'. Read-only - does not delete non-matching rows from the sheet.

data.name: find_replace
data.description: Find and replace text across a sheet or within a specific range.

data.name: merge_columns
data.description: Merges multiple columns of text into one (e.g. 'First Name' + 'Last Name' -> 'Full Name').

data.name: remove_duplicates
data.description: Removes duplicate rows within a range, based on all columns in that range.

data.name: set_autofilter
data.description: Turns on Excel's native AutoFilter dropdown arrows for a range's header row - the actual in-sheet filter UI, distinct from filter_data (which computes a filtered result without adding the interactive dropdowns).

data.name: sort_range
data.description: Sorts a range by one or more columns using Excel's own native Sort feature - matches the Data > Sort dialog exactly, including multi-level sorts. sort_columns: list of {'column_index': int, 'ascending': bool}, first item is primary sort key. Assumes row 1 of the range is a header.

data.name: split_column
data.description: Splits one column of text into multiple columns on a delimiter (e.g. 'Full Name' -> 'First Name', 'Last Name').

format.name: add_comment
format.description: Adds a cell comment/note - a small popup annotation attached to a cell, visible on hover. Tries the modern threaded-comment API first, falls back to a legacy note if unsupported on this Excel build.

format.name: add_hyperlink
format.description: Adds a clickable hyperlink to a cell - either a web URL or a link to another cell/sheet in this workbook.

format.name: apply_formatting
format.description: Applies bold, a number format (e.g. '$#,##0.00'), and/or a fill color to a range.

format.name: auto_fit_columns
format.description: Auto-fits column widths in a range so content isn't cut off.

format.name: color_scale_formatting
format.description: Applies a 2 or 3 color gradient scale across a range (e.g. red for low values, green for high).

format.name: conditional_formatting
format.description: Highlights cells matching a condition (e.g. greater_than 100 -> red fill).

format.name: data_bar_formatting
format.description: Applies in-cell data bars (a horizontal bar showing each value's size relative to the range) - like a mini bar chart inside the cells.

format.name: freeze_panes
format.description: Freezes rows/columns above and to the left of a cell (e.g. 'A2' freezes just the header row).

format.name: icon_set_formatting
format.description: Applies an icon set (e.g. traffic lights, arrows, stars) to a range based on relative value - style: '3TrafficLights1', '3Arrows', '5Stars', '3Symbols'.

format.name: set_page_layout
format.description: Configures print/page setup for a sheet: orientation, margins, fit-to-page scaling, and print area. Call this before export_to_pdf if the export needs to fit on a specific number of pages or be landscape - export_to_pdf uses whatever page setup is already on the sheet.

formatting.name: format_range
formatting.description: Formats a cell range with font styling (bold, size, color), background color, borders, number format, and text alignment. Makes data tables and dashboards look professional.

knowledge.name: search_knowledge_base
knowledge.description: Searches this user's stored company knowledge (previously ingested documents, manuals, SOPs, past reports) for passages relevant to a query. Use this before writing a report or answering a question that should reflect company-specific context rather than general knowledge.

read.name: get_excel_version
read.description: Detects the real Excel version and build on the user's machine, and reports whether it supports dynamic-array functions (UNIQUE, SORT, FILTER, XLOOKUP, LET). Call this once at the very start of a task before writing any formulas.

read.name: inspect_workbook
read.description: Builds a semantic map of one sheet, or audits the entire workbook when sheet_name is omitted. Reports used ranges, tables/charts/pivots, formulas, and every detected Excel formula error such as #REF! or #VALUE!. Always use the workbook-wide audit before reporting completion.

read.name: read_range
read.description: Reads values from a cell range so the agent can 'see' the data.

structure.name: clear_range
structure.description: Clears the contents and/or formatting of a range without deleting the cells themselves (unlike delete_row/delete_column, nothing shifts).

structure.name: combine_sheets
structure.description: Combines data from multiple sheets sharing the same column structure into one destination sheet, stacked vertically.

structure.name: copy_sheet
structure.description: Duplicates an existing sheet under a new name, keeping all its content and formatting.

structure.name: create_named_range
structure.description: Creates a named range so formulas elsewhere can reference it by name instead of raw coordinates.

structure.name: create_new_workbook
structure.description: Creates a brand-new, blank workbook and saves it at the given file path, making it the active workbook for subsequent skill calls in this task.

structure.name: create_sheet
structure.description: Creates a new, empty worksheet.

structure.name: create_sheets
structure.description: Creates and verifies multiple worksheets in the requested order in one Excel action.

structure.name: delete_column
structure.description: Deletes one or more entire columns from a sheet, shifting columns to the right leftward.

structure.name: delete_row
structure.description: Deletes one or more entire rows from a sheet, shifting rows below upward.

structure.name: delete_sheet
structure.description: Deletes a worksheet. Refuses if it's the only sheet in the workbook.

structure.name: group_rows_columns
structure.description: Groups a range of rows or columns into a collapsible outline section (the little +/- expand/collapse controls in the margin).

structure.name: insert_column
structure.description: Inserts one or more blank columns, shifting existing columns right.

structure.name: insert_row
structure.description: Inserts one or more blank rows, shifting existing rows down.

structure.name: merge_cells
structure.description: Merges a range of cells into one. Only the top-left cell's value is kept.

structure.name: open_workbook
structure.description: Opens an existing Excel file from disk by its full file path, making it the active workbook for subsequent skill calls in this task.

structure.name: rename_sheet
structure.description: Renames an existing worksheet.

structure.name: reorder_sheet
structure.description: Moves a sheet to a new tab position (0-indexed, left to right).

structure.name: set_sheet_visibility
structure.description: Hides or unhides a sheet (it still exists and can be referenced by formulas, just not shown in the tab bar).

structure.name: unmerge_cells
structure.description: Undoes a previous merge on a range of cells.

structure.name: unprotect_sheet
structure.description: Removes protection from a sheet that was locked with protect_sheet. Requires the same password it was protected with, if one was set.

transform.name: unpivot_data
transform.description: Transforms wide Excel data into a tall, normalized table.

vba.name: add_macro_button
vba.description: Draws a clickable Form-Control button on a sheet and wires it to run an existing macro by name. Create the macro first with create_vba_macro.

vba.name: check_vba_access
vba.description: Checks whether 'Trust access to the VBA project object model' is enabled in this Excel install. ALWAYS call this before create_vba_macro or add_macro_button - if it returns trusted: false, tell the user to enable it manually (File > Options > Trust Center > Trust Center Settings > Macro Settings > check 'Trust access to the VBA project object model') since this is a security setting the agent will not change on its own.

vba.name: create_vba_macro
vba.description: Adds a new VBA module to the workbook's VBA project and writes a real macro into it. Requires check_vba_access to return trusted: true first, and the workbook should be .xlsm/.xlsb (use save_as_macro_enabled if it's currently .xlsx) or the macro will be silently stripped on the next save.

vba.name: delete_vba_macro
vba.description: Removes an entire VBA module (and every macro inside it) from the workbook's VBA project. Deletes the whole module, not a single Sub within a module shared by others - use create_vba_macro with the same module_name to replace a module's contents instead if you only want to change one macro.

vba.name: list_vba_macros
vba.description: Lists every macro currently defined in the workbook's VBA project, so the AI can check what already exists before deciding to create a new one or reuse/edit an existing one. Requires check_vba_access to report trusted: true first.

vba.name: save_as_macro_enabled
vba.description: Saves the current workbook as a .xlsm (macro-enabled) file at the given path. Call this before create_vba_macro if the workbook is currently .xlsx, or Excel will silently discard any VBA code on save.

write.name: insert_formula
write.description: Writes a real, native Excel formula into a cell (e.g. '=SUM(A1:A10)'). Always use this for any calculated value - never write_cell with a precomputed number. Pass fill_to to safely fill one formula down a column and verify the full result range. Rejects blank results by default, invalid TableName! references, and whole-column ranges that can hang Excel.

write.name: write_cell
write.description: Writes a single literal value into a single cell (text/labels/raw input only - never a calculated value, use insert_formula for that).

write.name: write_table
write.description: Writes a structured table: a header row + data rows, starting at start_cell. Pass table_name to also convert it into a REAL native Excel Table - required for any later formula using TableName[ColumnName] structured references.

code_generation.use_when: No available skill or safe visible command can perform the specific operation, or a verified skill failure explicitly requested a focused code fallback.

name_box_and_shortcuts.raw_standard_chords: Validated conventional Ctrl/Shift/Alt chords are also accepted.

selection_policy.principle: There is no fixed tool order. For each atomic goal, choose the fastest safe available capability using the current workbook and UI evidence.
selection_policy.navigation_and_reveal: Use Name Box / Go To, sheet navigation shortcuts, or UI Automation to show and select the relevant sheet, range, or chart without taking a screenshot.
selection_policy.standard_visible_command: Use a documented shortcut or Ribbon KeyTip when it performs the whole command and the resulting dialog/object can be verified.
selection_policy.structured_excel_change: Use a dedicated skill/API when exact formulas, table structure, chart series, formatting, placement, or workbook verification matter.
selection_policy.chart_choice: For a simple selected source range, a verified chart shortcut is eligible. For an exact dashboard chart (series, title, layout, style, or placement), use the chart skill/API and visibly reveal the completed chart afterwards.
selection_policy.code_generation: Use only for a genuinely uncovered operation, a verified requested fallback, or large generated raw data that cannot fit a safe tool payload. Record why the other available routes are unsuitable.
selection_policy.verification: Read the workbook or popup back after every important change. A visible reveal does not replace workbook verification.

never: approve security, overwrite, protection, or link-update dialogs automatically
require: stop and report when no safe verified route remains

import random
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

wb = get_task_workbook()
sheet = wb.sheets['Sales Data']
sheet.clear()

headers = [
    "OrderID", "OrderDate", "CustomerName", "CustomerSegment", "Region", 
    "Salesperson", "ProductID", "ProductName", "Category", 
    "UnitsSold", "UnitPrice", "DiscountPercent", "Revenue", "Cost", "GrossProfit", "GrossMargin", "OrderStatus"
]
sheet.range("A1:Q1").value = headers

# Read products from Product Master for realistic product mapping
pm_sheet = wb.sheets['Product Master']
pm_data = pm_sheet.range("A2:I41").value

customers = [
    "Alpha Corp", "Beta LLC", "Gamma Inc", "Delta Retail", "Epsilon Group", 
    "Zeta Solutions", "Omega Tech", "Apex Industries", "Vertex Partners", "Pioneer Media",
    "Summit Enterprises", "Nova Systems", "Prime Logistics", "Beacon Financial", "Quantum Dynamics"
]
segments = ["Consumer", "SMB", "Enterprise"]
regions = ["North", "South", "East", "West"]
salespeople = ["Alice Smith", "Bob Jones", "Charlie Brown", "Diana Prince", "Ethan Hunt", "Fiona Gallagher"]
statuses = ["Completed", "Completed", "Completed", "Shipped", "Pending", "Cancelled"]

start_date = datetime(2024, 1, 1)
end_date = datetime(2025, 6, 30)
delta_days = (end_date - start_date).days

random.seed(42)
rows = []
for i in range(1, 351):
    order_id = f"ORD-{1000 + i}"
    rand_days = random.randint(0, delta_days)
    order_date = start_date + timedelta(days=rand_days)
    cust = random.choice(customers)
    seg = random.choice(segments)
    reg = random.choice(regions)
    sp = random.choice(salespeople)
    
    prod = random.choice(pm_data)
    prod_id = prod[0]
    prod_name = prod[1]
    cat = prod[2]
    std_price = prod[5]
    
    units = random.randint(1, 15)
    # price variation +- 5%
    unit_price = round(std_price * random.uniform(0.95, 1.05), 2)
    discount = round(random.choice([0.0, 0.0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15]), 2)
    status = random.choice(statuses)
    
    # We leave formulas for Revenue, Cost, GrossProfit, GrossMargin blank or place None so insert_formula handles them
    rows.append([
        order_id, order_date, cust, seg, reg, sp, prod_id, prod_name, cat, units, unit_price, discount, None, None, None, None, status
    ])

sheet.range("A2").value = rows
result = {"verified": True, "verification_note": "Generated 350 sales transactions successfully."}
